### ① Derived judgments

1. File surface. One commit (c2236e37, author Claude, PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`, trailers `Co-Authored-By: Claude` + `Claude-Session:`, no model identifier). `git diff --stat d79eecfe5b c2236e3772`, the REST file listing (+27 / −4, 4 files) and the PR body agree on exactly four paths: `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` +1/−1 (464 → 464 lines), `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` +3/−3 (487 → 487), `docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md` +12/−0 and `.changeset/29506-title-format-refused-teaching.md` +11/−0 (new). Nothing else is touched; the ratchet script is not in the diff. Correct, and on surface.
2. The refusal the two rows assert, read at the merge-base (PR #29499's merge `3557366c02` is an ancestor of d79eecfe5b). `validateTitleFormatRetired` (validate-record-title.ts L75–97) returns one finding per declaring object with `severity: 'error'` and `rule: TITLE_FORMAT_RETIRED` = `'title-format-retired'` (L39); its registration (authoring-rules.ts L1563–1572) is `tier: 'gating'`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME` (= `['cli', 'runtime-publish']`, L476), `runtimeTypes: ['object']`, `commands: ALL`, so the same rule runs under `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` and at the runtime publish gate. The pins: validate-record-title.test.ts L59–66 ("REFUSES (errors) when titleFormat is declared — ruling of record 6574393684, letter B", `severity` `'error'`); runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts L461–468 ("REFUSES an object that declares a titleFormat (validateTitleFormatRetired)", the single refusal `title-format-retired`) and L471–481 (the re-save of a stored object carrying it is refused too); protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts L938–972 (a stored object carrying the key: still read, `code: 'INVALID_METADATA', status: 422` on its next save, clean once the key is dropped); validate-title-format-retired.test.ts L86–97 (`os validate` exits 1 with `title-format-retired`, and the `nameField` control validates clean). So "a save and `os validate` refuse it (`title-format-retired`)" and "Move it to `nameField`" are each the code's own words; the diagnostic's name is exactly `title-format-retired`. Correct.
3. What `os explain title-format-retired` prints (rule-explanations.ts L3078–3100, wired through explain.ts L7/L508): paragraph 1 carries the render-only reason ("`titleFormat` is a render-only template: the server can neither return the title it draws nor query by it, the shared title predicate (`objectTitleCompleteness`) never reads it, and an explicit `nameField` takes precedence over it"), paragraph 2 the migration and the refusal doors, paragraph 3 "An error, not a warning, though the schema still parses the key … A draft save passes; its publish is refused." The test at validate-record-title.test.ts L168–193 pins seven of those facts by substring, among them `render-only template`, `neither return the title it draws nor query by it` and `an explicit \`nameField\` takes precedence`. So both facts the data row drops — the render-only reason and "(it wins)" — have a pinned home in the explanation the lint `fix:` line points at (the `[#22161]` comment, L86–87), and a second home in ADR-0079 D3's body ("an explicit `nameField` takes precedence over it", L141–142, unchanged by this PR) and in the `titleFormat` describe itself (object.zod.ts L3404). Correct.
4. The data row, merge-base L90 → head L90 (192 → 181 bytes). Old: "**Deprecated, not removed (ADR-0079)** — render-only: the server can't return or query it. Use `nameField` (it wins); a composite title follows the `nameField` row". New: "**Refused (ADR-0079)**: a save and `os validate` refuse it (`title-format-retired`). Move it to `nameField`; a composite title follows the `nameField` row". "Deprecated, not removed" was false after #29499 for the only reader this row has — an author deciding whether to write the key — and the new wording states the two doors the code names and the diagnostic to grep. The dropped render-only clause is a reason, not a rule: the row's rule (do not write it; write `nameField`) survives and is now stronger, and the reason has the homes in ①.3; within the skill, the `nameField` row directly above (L88) still carries "a text formula is display-only", the half of the reason an author acts on. "(it wins)" is still true at runtime (the ruling's "not honoured" arm: `provisionPrimary` keeps stamping the pointer, the explanation says the pointer takes precedence) but no longer decides anything an author can write: a new definition carrying both keys is refused before precedence is consulted, and a stored legacy row carrying both is served by the pointer whichever way the author reads the row. Its two homes (①.3) are pinned. lanes/skills.md's test — a cut whose content has no other home loses a rule — is met: neither cut is a rule, and both have homes. Ruling 6513306068's same-file-deletion path is the gate-recognised way to MOVE a ceiling row; no ceiling row moves here (①.7), so that path is not invoked and a home outside the file is not a question this PR raises. Correct.

The carriers cell goes from "`Object.titleFormat` (deprecated → `nameField`, ADR-0079)" to "`Object.titleFormat` (a save and `os validate` refuse it; move it to `nameField`, ADR-0079)": the same two facts as the data row, in the cell that lists where a template may be written, which is exactly where an author would otherwise learn the key is still a legal carrier. The cut sentence, "a template holds a path and a formatter, nothing else.", restates the same row's Grammar cell — "`{{ path }}` or `{{ path \| formatter[:arg] }}` — double braces only, no conditionals" — which is byte-identical on both trees and names the two things a template may hold and the one it may not; the instruction the sentence used to motivate, "Move logic into a CEL field", survives with its colon turned into a period. No test under `packages/**`, `scripts/**` or `skills/**` pins the cut sentence (grep: zero hits for `holds a path and a formatter`). The lines around the cut are otherwise unchanged (①.7). Correct.

7. The D8 clause. D8 (L235–248) says `validate-record-title` "reports two warnings — `title-format-retired` (D3) and `title-unresolvable` … — and **never errors**", quoting a sentence of validate-record-title.ts ("Both are warnings…") that no longer exists in that file (the head's module note says the two rules "sit on different tiers", L26–27). After #29499 the first half of D8 is false and the second half (`title-unresolvable` is a warning, `validateRecordTitle` never errors) is still true. The amendment's "D8's 'never errors' no longer covers this rule" is therefore accurate and narrow: it names the one rule the ruling moved and leaves `title-unresolvable` under D8. On scope: the card asked for "a dated amendment note at D3"; the D8 clause sits inside that note, edits no line of D8, and records a consequence of the same ruling and the same PR — without it, a reader of D3 would find D8 contradicting the amendment two sections down, which is the "decision nobody can find" Prime Directive 13 warns of. On whether an amendment may touch D8: `docs/adr/**` is Tier H governed text, so the whole file lands on a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval, and the ruling itself (not this PR) is what changed D8's truth; the note records, it does not decide. What the clause does not do is leave a pointer AT D8, so a reader who lands on D8 by its anchor still reads an unqualified "never errors" and a quotation the cited file no longer carries, and the ADR's status line (L3: "Accepted — implemented") still names no amendment although docs/adr/README.md L8 makes that line "the single fact" the index is generated from and ADR-0015 / ADR-0035 / ADR-0045 / ADR-0050 / ADR-0055 record their inline amendments there: S1 (④). Folded into S1 as the cheapest place to say so, not a separate card.

### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (an author or agent reading the skill must learn that a save and `os validate` refuse `titleFormat`, and what to write instead; a reader of ADR-0079 must not find D3 still calling the diagnostic advisory) and the code on `main`:

- `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`, the `titleFormat` row: the row is the one place an author looks up whether the key may be written, and "Refused … a save and `os validate` refuse it (`title-format-retired`). Move it to `nameField`" is the shortest true answer — the two doors the code names, the diagnostic to grep, the prescription, and the pointer to the composite-title case in the row above. The two dropped clauses are reasons the row's reader no longer acts on, with pinned homes where the refusal sends them. Holds.
